question.text: As per the SEBI (AIF) (Amendment) Regulations applicable to Manager key-investment-team certifications, which of the following is correct for a Category II AIF Manager (not an AI-only Fund)?

answer.text: At least one KMP must hold the NISM-Series-XIX-C OR NISM-Series-XIX-D certification
All KMPs of the Manager must hold NISM-Series-XV Research Analyst certification
Only the Sponsor's director needs certification; Manager KMPs are exempt
Certification is optional for LVFs only

explanation.text: The Logic: As per SEBI (AIF) (Amendment) Regulations, 2020 (w.e.f. Oct 19, 2020), at least one key personnel amongst the associated persons functioning in the key investment team of the Manager of a Cat I/II AIF shall have NISM-Series-XIX-C (All-Cat AIF Managers) OR NISM-Series-XIX-D (Cat I and II AIF Managers) certification. This requirement does not apply to AI-only Funds (per Third Amendment, 2025). Additionally, at least one key personnel must have a qualifying finance/economics/commerce degree or CFA — both conditions can be met by the same person. The Trap: Option B confuses with Research Analyst regime. Option C is incorrect — Manager team (not Sponsor) is the certification subject. Option D inverts the AI-only exemption (AI-only funds are EXEMPT, not other funds). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers the certification mandate in detail (the exam itself authorises all-cat). XV Research Analyst is a different certification for research work. XXI-B Portfolio Manager certification is separate for PMS. Upon expiry, personnel must obtain fresh certification — keep tracking renewal dates. Manager's Pro-Tip: Build a compliance calendar tracking each KMP's certification validity — SEBI inspectors check this during triennial inspections. If the lone certified personnel leaves, you have a brief window to re-certify another KMP or hire a certified professional. Treat this as single-point-of-failure risk.
